audit.whatIsWrong: early claims 'Rumble has no ability until he hits Flamespitter at 1', which is self-contradictory, and whys[1] says he 'unlocks Flamespitter at 2'.
audit.why: Rumble picks an ability at level 1 like everyone else; the real level-1 truth is that Flamespitter is a 600-range cone, so he must walk into Decimating Smash range to use it.
audit.corrected: Rewrote early and whys[0]/whys[1] around the 600-range cone requirement instead of a false unlock timing.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart disagreed with its own whys: win[3] (Levels 4-5) said Sion while whys[3] describes Rumble winning that window, and win[4] (Level 6) said Rumble while whys[4] describes Unstoppable Onslaught flipping it to you. win[5] said Skill while whys[5] describes you out-bulking him at Heartsteel.
audit.why: The rows were shifted by one relative to the explanations, and the 54.3% win rate supports Sion owning level 6 and the first-item spike.
audit.corrected: win[3] -> Rumble, win[4] -> Sion, win[5] -> Sion, proposed as one atomic group. No full-layer entry exists for this matchup, so there are no phases[].side rows to pair.

audit.whatIsWrong: late called Rumble's ult 'His Equalizer' and wants.foe[2] called it 'Drop Equalizer'; the terrain-cuts-retreat interaction was absent everywhere.
audit.why: The ability is The Equalizer (R, 130/105/80s). It lays a damaging, slowing line across the ground; Sion has no dash, so a line dropped on his retreat path is a hard commitment of Flash.
audit.corrected: Real name used in late and wants.foe[2]; added the no-dash / hold-Flash-for-the-line point to late. Also replaced generic 'E-armor-shred' with Roar of the Slayer and 'W-shield' with Soul Furnace.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing stated about Soul Furnace's 3-second delay against a damage-over-time cone.
audit.why: Flamespitter burns for 3 seconds; the shield can only be reactivated after 3 seconds, so the detonation lands as the cone expires rather than during it.
sources: kit text for both W abilities

edits.before: You are slow to charge Q at level 1 but Rumble has no ability either — a full knockup before he steps up wins the first trade and forces an early W spend on his side.
edits.after: You are slow to charge Q at level 1, but Flamespitter is a 600-range cone — he has to walk into the arc, and a full knockup as he steps up wins the trade and burns his Scrap Shield.

edits.before: Rumble unlocks Flamespitter at 2 and immediately out-DPSes you in a sustained trade; your W-shield is online but his DoT ticks through a clean shield detonation window.
edits.after: With Flamespitter and a harpoon both up he out-DPSes you in a sustained trade; Soul Furnace is online, but his cone keeps burning through the three seconds before you can detonate it.

edits.before: Drop Equalizer on your retreat path to zone you off the wave and deny a clean return to base
edits.after: Drop The Equalizer across your retreat path to zone you off the wave — you have no dash out

edits.before: Level 1 is yours if you can set up the charge — Rumble has no ability until he hits Flamespitter at 1, and a max-charge Q knockup before he closes the gap sends him back to tower with no way to punish you. Respect the walk-up angle though: if he gets his nose under yours before you finish charging, Flamespitter ticks through your body and he wins the damage race at that range. Take W at level 2 so his first real Flamespitter rotation hits your Soul Furnace shield rather than your health bar, then detonate the shield into him after absorbing the bulk of the burn — you trade magic for physical and come out ahead.
edits.after: Level 1 is yours if you can set up the charge — Flamespitter only reaches 600 units, so he has to walk into the Decimating Smash arc to use it, and a max-charge knockup as he steps up sends him back to tower with no way to punish you. Respect the walk-up angle though: if he gets his nose under yours before you finish charging, the cone burns through your body and he wins the damage race at that range. Take W at level 2 so his first real Flamespitter hits Soul Furnace rather than your health bar, then detonate the shield into him after absorbing the bulk of the burn — you trade magic for physical and come out ahead.

edits.before: At Heartsteel you out-stat him cleanly. Your W-shield now absorbs an entire Flamespitter rotation with HP to spare, your HP passive has been compounding since the laning kills, and his percent-HP DoT — which was scary at 3,000 HP — barely dents 6,000. Land E-armor-shred first to reduce his resistance to your Decimating Smash knockup, then chase him down; your passive zombie remains a genuine kill threat even if he somehow gets you low, which keeps him honest about when he can walk forward. His Equalizer is still the lane's biggest equalizer: never stand in a line with him casting, as a full-duration Equalizer into your HP bar does set the clock back meaningfully.
edits.after: At Heartsteel you out-stat him cleanly. Soul Furnace now absorbs an entire Flamespitter rotation with HP to spare, your HP passive has been compounding since the laning kills, and his magic DoT — which was scary at 3,000 HP — barely dents 6,000. Land Roar of the Slayer first to strip his armour ahead of the Decimating Smash knockup, then chase; your passive zombie stays a genuine kill threat even if he gets you low, which keeps him honest about walking forward. The Equalizer is still the biggest swing: it is a slowing line laid across your escape on an 80-second cooldown at rank 3, and you have no dash — hold Flash for crossing it, not for the damage.

notes: The _missing entry for this matchup lists Scrap Shield (W) as a retreat-cutting terrain effect. Riot's own text says Scrap Shield only shields and grants move speed — the terrain/knockup flags on Rumble's W look like tooltip-parsing misfires. I used only The Equalizer for the terrain-cuts-retreat point. Rumble's E is listed at a 0.5s cooldown with 2 stored charges, so treating it as a spammable slow rather than a punishable cooldown is correct; I did not write a cooldown-window claim about it. No full-layer entry exists for sion vs rumble (currentText.full is null), so all edits are content-layer and no phases[].side pairing was possible.
